This Crl.M.C has been filed challenging Annexure I common order passed by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-III, Perumbavoor (for short, the trial court) in CMP Nos.435 and 452/2019.
2.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-III, Perumbavoor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The Kottappady police registered Crime No.54/19 against one Sujith under Sections 406, 420,
376, 313, 323 of the IPC and Section 119(b) of the Kerala Police Act, 2011 on the complaint made by the defacto complainant who has been arrayed as the 2nd respondent in this Crl.M.C.
3.
The prosecution allegation is that, the accused raped the victim/2nd respondent under the pretext of marriage and misappropriated her money and gold ornaments.
During the investigation of the crime, 67.900 grams of gold ornaments allegedly belonging to the 2nd respondent were seized from the proprietorship concern of the petitioner.
The petitioner was running a private bank namely M/s Kakkattu Financiers.
The accused and the 2nd respondent together came to his private bank and pledged the above mentioned gold ornaments.
The petitioner preferred CMP No.435/2019 and the 2nd respondent preferred CMP No.452/2019 under Section 452 of Cr.P.C for the 2025:KER:39247 release of the gold ornaments on interim custody.
The trial court after hearing both sides allowed CMP No.452/2019 and dismissed CMP No.435/2019 as per Annexure I common order.
The gold ornaments were ordered to be released to the 2 nd respondent.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Prosecutor.
There is no appearance for the 2nd respondent.
5. It is not in dispute that the gold ornaments weighing 67.900 grams, seized by the police in connection with Crime No.54/2019 were pledged at the petitioner's bank for 1,50,000/-.
Annexure E is the application given by the accused Sujith for pledging the gold ornaments with the petitioner.
Anenxure F is the gold loan ledger which would show that Sri. Sujith received 1,50,000/- from the petitioner.
According to the petitioner, the 2nd respondent and Sri. Sujith came together and pledged the gold ornaments and accepted money from him.

It is denied by the 2 nd respondent who contended that the accused dishonestly procured the gold ornaments from her and pledged the same with the petitioner and she, being the actual owner, is entitled to get back the gold ornaments.

sentences.text: From the rival contentions, it is clear that the petitioner was in lawful custody of the gold ornaments.
The gold ornaments were lawfully pledged with the petitioner.
Annexures E and F would prove the same.
The trial court believed the version of the 2nd respondent that Sri. Sujith procured gold ornaments dishonestly and pledged with the petitioner.
However, the trial court did not consider Annexure B written complaint filed by the 2nd respondent before the Superintendent of Police, Aluva.
In the said complaint it is clearly stated that she had handed over the gold ornaments to Sri. Sujith for the purpose of pledging.
Thus, it is clear that the gold ornaments were handed over by the 2 nd respondent to Sri.Sujith, who pledged the same with the petitioner with the consent of the 2nd respondent.
The 2nd respondent has no case that the loan amount of 1,50,000/- has been repaid to the petitioner.
So long as the loan amount is not repaid, the petitioner has lien over the gold ornaments.

A Single Bench of this Court in Vypeen Kuries & Finance V. State of Kerala (2015 SCC OnLine Ker 30965) has held that, when gold ornaments are seized in connection with the investigation from a banking institution engaged in banking business through a validly procured licence, such a banking institution from where 2025:KER:39247 gold is seized, is the person entitled to the custody of the same.

entities.text: Vypeen Kuries & Finance V. State of Kerala (2015 SCC OnLine Ker 30965)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. For the reasons stated above, I am of the view that the petitioner is entitled to the interim custody of the gold ornaments.
Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside.

The gold ornaments shall be given to the petitioner on the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall execute a bond of 2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakhs only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each.
(ii) The petitioner shall not sell or melt the gold ornaments so as to change its identity or alienate the same without the order of the court.
(iii) The petitioner shall produce the gold ornaments as and when directed.
(iv) The Junior Superintendent of the trial court is directed to take a photograph of the gold ornaments before handing over the same to the petitioner.
The Crl.M.C. is disposed of as above.
